flags.quote: taking the pawn on e6 with your d5-bishop puts it where the black rook and pawn can take and you lose a knight
flags.critique: White has no knights left. I hung a bishop on e6 to the rook — say that. Calling it a knight makes me distrust every tactic label after this. Also b4 is named as better with zero idea: it kicks the queen on c5.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c6 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: This is a recapture. Bishop for the knight that just died on c6 is equal, not 'a bishop ahead.' I am not winning a piece here. If the queen now looks at d6, say 'discovered attack on d6' — don't invent material.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c6 with your b7-bishop is the strongest move because you come out a pawn ahead.
flags.critique: Bishop takes knight. That's an even trade. The extra pawn is next move, when the recapture on c6 hangs. Telling me I'm already a pawn up teaches me to miscount in every exchange.

flags.quote: taking the knight on c3 with your g7-bishop would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook
flags.critique: Bxc3+ is a capture with check that doubles White's pawns. There is no pin. You already used 'pin the pawn to the rook' for Bg7 two moves ago, and now you're gluing it onto a completely different tactic. Teach check and wrecked structure, or don't suggest the move.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I just recaptured in a pawn trade. Black's pawn on d5 was not a free lunch — we swapped c-pawns. 'Undefended' plus a wins-material reason on an equal recapture is a lie.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to g7 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I fianchettoed. That's development, king-side, and the long diagonal. A relative pin of b2 to a1 is a trivia fact, not the lesson. After this I think every bishop move is 'a pin.'

flags.quote: Taking the rook on c5 with your queen keeps you winning because the rook was undefended and then pin the pawn to the king. A better move would have been taking the rook on c5 with your d-pawn because it saves your queen from capture.
flags.critique: This is a mistake that dumps a plus-two advantage, and you opened with 'keeps you winning.' The sentence also breaks English: 'and then pin the pawn.' Recapture with the pawn, not the queen — that's the lesson. 'Saves your queen from capture' sounds like the queen was hanging before I moved it.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on c5 with your c1-rook is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black queen.
flags.critique: The rook on c5 is not defending the queen. It's a rook trade on the open file. 'Removed defender of the queen' is a template hallucination. I needed: you win the exchange of the rook that just sat on c5.

flags.quote: Moving your a1-rook to c1 leaves your pawn hanging to the black bishop. A better move would have been moving your pawn to b4 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Lichess called this a blunder (−185). You called it a mistake. b4 kicks the rook on c5; it does not save a pawn from Bg7. If b2 was already hanging, Rc1 didn't create that. Give me the kick, not a fake save.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h4 is the strongest move because it saves your bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Qc5 already looks at Bg5 on the 5th rank. Pushing h4 does not defend g5 and it occupies the bishop's retreat square. If Qxg5 isn't free, say why. 'Saves your bishop' is just false.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Which pawn? d5 is the move, not the victim. Bb7 was eating e4 along the long diagonal; d5 slams the door shut. Teach 'blunt the Owen bishop / stop Bxe4,' not a nameless save.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: e6 hits the monster bishop on d5 that is pinning f7 to my king. That's a pawn kick, not king safety. e6 actually pokes holes around the king. You picked the one reason that isn't the point.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d5 with your b3-bishop is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and then pin the pawn to the king.
flags.critique: Recapturing a knight you can take is not a thriller, and 'and then pin the pawn' isn't a sentence. If the bishop on d5 pins f7 to the king, say 'this recapture pins the f-pawn to the king.' Don't staple two templates together.

flags.quote: Moving your c2-bishop to b3 is the strongest move because it saves your b3-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The piece is on c2. It becomes the b3-bishop after I move. This reads like you're saving a ghost. The real idea: get off the c-file before Black's queen-and-rook battery takes the bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-rook to c5 is a mistake, but moving your c6-rook to c7 would be better.
flags.critique: Why is c5 wrong? Why is c7 right? Lichess says inaccuracy, you say mistake. A 1200 needs 'this rook gets kicked / hangs / leaves a file,' not two squares and a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your d4-knight to c6 puts it at risk of attack from the black c8-rook and b7-bishop. A better move would have been moving your pawn to a4.
flags.critique: Attacked twice, defended once by d5 — that's hanging, not 'at risk.' Then you prescribe a4 like a magic word. If the lesson is don't park a knight on a square the rook and bishop both eat, stop there. Don't tack on an unexplained pawn move.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to d5 is playable, but moving your pawn to a4 would be better.
flags.critique: a4 again, still no because. Nd5 looks like a dream outpost to me. If the engine wants a queenside restraint, tell me what a4 stops. 'There's better' plus a SAN is not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to b7 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: This is the Owen move: the bishop stares at e4. I am not occupying the center; I am sniping it. 'Claim more of the center' is the same sentence you used for d4. Teach the diagonal.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Reasons include hanging and doubled pawns, and you printed none of that. d5 is defended; this is a central break, not picking up a stray. Either say 'you challenge the d5 wedge' or don't fire hanging on a protected pawn.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d5 with your f6-knight is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your bishop on the white pawn.
flags.critique: I took their best-placed knight. That's the news. A discovered glance at b2 is garnish. Don't make me hunt which white pawn — name b2 or drop it.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No reason, and eval jumped +50 for White, but you still called it strongest. This is Owen's Defense: prepare Bb7. If you can't say that, don't call a second-rate opening move 'the one.'

flags.quote: Moving your c1-bishop to g5 is playable, but moving your g1-knight to e2 would be better.
flags.critique: There's a pin reason in the dump and you didn't use it — and Black has no knight on f6 to pin anyway. Why is Nge2 better? Develop without a cheap target? Support d4? I got a SAN and 'There's better.'

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The only reason tagged is backward_pawn, which never reaches the sentence. c4 supports d5 and grabs space. Don't attach 'backward pawn' to a space-gaining move and then say nothing.

flags.quote: Moving your g8-knight to f6 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: I developed a knight toward the center and toward castling. king_safer is a side effect, not the idea. Same lazy bucket you used for e6 later. Call it development.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on f6 with your bishop is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: They offered a bishop trade and I took. If Bf6 was hitting h4, name h4. 'Saves your pawn' on a recapture is the same save-template overuse as Bb3 and h4. I already know how trades work — tell me which pawn, or that the trade is forced.

suggestions.title: Do not call recaptures winning material
suggestions.detail: pickBenefitReasons emits wins_material whenever capturedSeeCp >= 80, so cxd5 recaptures, Bxc6 (B=N), and dxc6 all get 'undefended' / 'a pawn ahead' / 'a bishop ahead.' Gate wins_material on net change after a plausible recapture, or skip it when the captured unit just arrived on that square. A 1200 notices immediately when an even trade is sold as loot.

suggestions.title: Name the hung piece, not a cp bucket
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 250+ cp to 'a knight' and 200–249 to 'a bishop,' so a hung bishop (~300–330) becomes 'you lose a knight' (ply 41, and White had zero knights). hangingLossCopy should use reason.piece.type. Same bug makes 'come out a bishop ahead' vs 'a pawn ahead' drift off the actual swap.

suggestions.title: Don't lead with relative pins
suggestions.detail: selectBecauseReasons prefers any tactical kind, so a b2-to-rook relative pin beats fianchetto on Bg7, and the same pin phrase is reused as the because for Bxc3+. Rank check, capture, and doubled pawns above incidental relative pins; drop pin from the because-slot when the pinner is a developing fianchetto and the pinned unit is a safe pawn.

suggestions.title: Give the alternative a real because
suggestions.detail: Nge2, a4 (twice), Rc7, b4, and dxc5 show up as 'would be better' with empty or wrong suggestedBecause (saves a pawn, saves the queen). Contrast from the suggested move's own effects: a4/b4 as pawn kicks, dxc5 as recapturing with a pawn so the queen stays home. Empty suggestedBecause is how you get 'There's better' plus a SAN.

suggestions.title: Stop printing strongest-move with no because
suggestions.detail: b6, g6, d6, h3, Re8, Bc2, Nd4, a6, Qc8, Bf6 and others are 'the strongest move' with reasons []. Add cheap detectors: fianchetto (b6/g6/Bb7/Bg7), pawn-break (c6/e6), prophylaxis/luft (h3), centralization/outpost (Nd4/Nd5). Better a modest plan sentence than a blank verdict plus 'That's the one.'

suggestions.title: Keep 'is a mistake' on teachable misses
suggestions.detail: verdictClause lets still_winning replace the classification when concept is capture, so Qxc5 (129 cp, Lichess Mistake) reads 'keeps you winning.' Eval frame should be a lead ('you are still winning, but…') like still_losing already is, never the verdict for inaccuracy/mistake/blunder.

suggestions.title: Make 'and then' clauses finite verbs
suggestions.detail: describeBecause concatenates two tactics as 'X and then Y' while pin follow-up is 'then pin the pawn to the king' — result: 'the knight was undefended and then pin the pawn' (plies 35, 40). Follow-up copy needs a subject ('then you pin') or drop the second tactic when it isn't a real continuation of the first.

suggestions.title: Don't steal pawn kicks for king safety
suggestions.detail: king_safer won Ngf6 (a developing knight) and e6 (kicking Bd5 / breaking the f7 pin). If the move attacks a minor piece with a pawn, or is a standard developing knight hop, rank that above king_safer. 1200s need 'kick the bishop' and 'develop,' not a vibes-based safer king.

whatWorked: Both castles actually taught the two jobs: king tucks away, rook comes in.
Rc8 naming the open file was a real positional lesson, not 'the strongest move.'
Nc6 at least named the c8-rook and b7-bishop as the attackers (even if 'at risk' is soft).
Rxc6 'the pawn was undefended' is the actual extra-pawn moment — the one ply 28 stole.
Rxe6 'the bishop was undefended' after the Bxe6 blunder is the clean take-the-piece line.
